Armed Conflict & Security

• Russia intensified strikes on Kyiv and its suburbs, disrupting daily life as air defenses and residents face near-continuous alerts.
• Iran-linked attacks into Jordan have tested Amman’s security ties with the US, while a deadly strike on a wedding in Iran’s Hormozgan province spurred local outrage.
• In Nepal’s flood zones, rescuers pulled workers alive from a hydropower tunnel more than a week after flash floods; the country faces a vast recovery effort.
• Pakistan overhauled its military command structure for the first time in decades, expanding the army chief’s powers amid questions over civilian oversight.

Armed Conflict & Security.title: Iranian strikes on Jordan test the bonds between the US and one of its staunchest Mideast allies
Armed Conflict & Security.text:
President Donald Trump greets Jordan's King Abdullah II at the White House, Tuesday, Feb. 11, 2025, in Washington. (AP Photo/Evan Vucci, File)2026-09-04T05:01:14Z
                                        Jordan, a staunch U.S. ally that hosts American forces in the Mideast, has paid a price for its relationship with Washington, which has made the kingdom’s military bases a target of repeat Iranian strikes.Hundreds of drone and missile attacks have added to other strains on Jordan that include a slumping economy and volatility in the neighboring West Bank, where Israeli settlers have ramped up attacks on Palestinians.Despite the risk of more strikes, Jordanian leaders say they are committed to maintaining the relationship after decades of courting deeper security ties with American officials and offering to be a reliable partner with the West in a region rocked by conflict. Analysts say the alliance offers Jordan a way to guard against Iran’s attempts to destabilize its neighbors.King Abdullah II of Jordan seemed to acknowledge the need for such alliances last year, when he warned that destabilization fueled by the COVID-19 crisis, Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine and multiple Israeli military campaigns in the Middle East could trigger chaos far beyond the region.“We are living through wave after wave of disruption, without pause,” he told European lawmakers. “There is no telling where the boundaries of this battleground will end. That, my friends, is a threat to people everywhere.”
    
        
    

Jordan embraces Washington to weather stormy Middle EastThe Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan is a puzzle-piece-shaped nation bordering Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Syria, Israel and the West Bank. More than 11 million Jordanians live between the Jordan River, the Red Sea and eastern deserts strewn with ruins.Besides the threat from Iran, Jordan faces other challenges, such as an economy that has buckled under millions of refugees fleeing regional conflicts. Soaring energy prices and inflation have added to the burden as the tourism sector struggles to draw visitors to landscapes lionized in Hollywood by Peter O’Toole, Harrison Ford and Matt Damon.And next door, growing Israeli settler violence in the West Bank is deeply unsettling to Jordanians who fear instability could drive many of the 2.8 million Palestinians there to flee into the kingdom, said Sean Yom, a professor at Temple University and author of a 2025 book titled “Jordan: Politics in an Accidental Crucible.”

Since taking the reins from his father, King Hussein, in 1999, Abdullah has forged ever-stronger links between his capital, Amman, and Washington. The monarch — a fluent English speaker whose dynasty claims to be descended from the Prophet Muhammad — enjoys widespread support among world leaders and Democratic and Republican lawmakers in the U.S.
    
        
            
                
                    
    
    


    

  

  
    Read More 
  
  

    
    
    
  

    
        
    

                
            
        
    
President Donald Trump once called the king “one of the true great leaders of the world.” Joe Biden also praised his leadership. First lady Jill Biden was a guest at the wedding of Abdullah’s son Hussein to a Saudi aristocrat in 2023. Pope Leo welcomed Abdullah to the Vatican in 2025.
    
        
    

As part of its partnership with the West, Jordan provided logistical help and intelligence for the U.S.-led 2003 invasion of Iraq, and it contributed to the fight against Islamic State militants in Syria and Iraq.

Amer Sabaileh, an independent Jordanian political analyst, said Jordan’s alliance with the U.S. is central to Abdullah’s yearslong campaign to secure his kingdom against danger, including from Iran.
    
        
    

Jordanian elites see Iran’s support of Shiite militias in Iraq, armed Palestinian groups and Syrian drug traffickers as direct threats to the royal court, Yom said.“Very few people in Jordan think the Islamic Republic is good for the Middle East,” he said.US military operations rely on a dozen sites in JordanAmman and Washington signed a defense-cooperation agreement in 2021 that granted U.S. forces and contractors access to 12 military installations across the kingdom. The NATO military alliance opened its first liaison office in the region in Jordan in 2025.In the run-up to the Iran war, Jordan’s sprawling Muwaffaq Salti Air Base became “a key logistics hub” for U.S. C-17 transport planes and about 60 combat aircraft, said David Schenker, a fellow at the Washington Institute.
    
        
    

“Jordan provides great strategic depth,” he said, calling the kingdom’s position “essential” to the U.S. campaign against Iran. “This makes Jordan a target, not just targeting U.S. forces but also targeting the king.”About 50,000 U.S. troops are currently deployed across the Middle East, with an unknown number in Jordan. Schenker estimates that at least 8%, or $1.47 billion, of the kingdom’s annual budget comes directly from U.S. grants.Adm. Charles Bradford, commander of the Pentagon department covering the Middle East, said in May that the U.S. military had relocated personnel and assets from its mission against the Islamic State from Iraq to Jordan. The shift was part of a broader, long-running strategy to put more distance between American forces and Iranian missiles.Those troops were enough to draw fire to Jordan from the Islamic Republic. Most of the incoming missiles and drones were knocked down by U.S. air defenses.Speaking Thursday in Vienna, Jordanian Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi defended his country’s right to make its own decisions.
    
        
    

“Iran has been attacking us and many other countries in the region long before even this war started,” he said, referring to Iranian “meddling in internal affairs” and other clandestine efforts. “So we do not buy their argument. We are a sovereign country. We were not a party to this war.”___Associated Press video journalist Philipp-Moritz Jenne contributed to this report.

A nozzle pumps diesel into the fuel tank of bus in Orange, Calif., Tuesday, April 7, 2026. (AP Photo/Jae C. Hong, File)2026-09-04T08:37:59Z
                                        CHICAGO (AP) — Diesel hit a new record price in the U.S. on Friday, soaring to an average of $5.85 a gallon for the first time ever as the 6-month-long war with Iran continues to disrupt the world’s flow of fuel.Because diesel is used for many freight and delivery networks, higher diesel prices mean higher transportation costs for a long list of everyday goods. More expensive fuel is increasing bills for businesses across sectors — some of which have already passed off costs to consumers in the form of added fees on online orders and packages in the mail. And shoppers may see more and more sticker shock trickle into store shelves.One of the most immediate strains falls in the grocery aisle, particularly with produce, meat and other perishable foods that need to be hauled in and restocked frequently — or even harvested using diesel-powered farm equipment. It can take time for all of those costs to trickle down. Still, experts warn that price hikes could mount the longer diesel remains expensive. A range of other products are also transported by diesel trucks, trains and boats, including clothing, cosmetics, furniture and more.

Geopolitics & Diplomacy.text:
A Red Cross convoy passes a Lebanese checkpoint near the border with Israel in the southern village of Mansouri, Lebanon, Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. (AP Photo/Mohammed Zaatari) CORRECTION: A Red Cross convoy, instead of U.N. peacekeeper convoy2026-09-04T08:59:50Z
                                        TYRE, Lebanon (AP) — Four prisoners from Lebanon held in Israel were released and handed over to Lebanese authorities via the International Committee of the Red Cross Friday as part of a deal between the two countries. In return, Lebanon agreed to search for the bodies of Jewish Lebanese citizens who went missing during the country’s civil war decades ago.Dozens of Lebanese prisoners are believed to be held in Israeli detention centers, including civilians as well as Hezbollah militants captured during fighting in southern Lebanon. A total of five detainees were released under the current deal, all civilians.The first Lebanese prisoner, identified as Malek Ghazi, was released to the International Committee of the Red Cross and then to the Lebanese army on Thursday.Associated Press journalists waiting at a checkpoint south of the city of Tyre in southern Lebanon saw a convoy of ICRC vehicles heading toward the Naqoura border crossing Friday morning and later return. The convoy then entered a Lebanese army barracks in Tyre.
    
        
    

Mahmoud Ayash, the brother of prisoner Hussein Ayash from the village of Harouf, who was waiting there, said his brother had been detained for about three months and had called from the border crossing in Naqoura to say that he had been released and was with the ICRC.“I hope all our prisoners in Israeli prisons will be released and for all Lebanese citizens to be liberated,” he said.


    
        




    


Ahmed Atwe, also waiting at the checkpoint, said his relative, Mohammed Juheir, was a fisherman from the border town of Naqoura who was captured at sea by Israeli forces a year ago, when a ceasefire agreement was in place.

The ICRC said in a statement that the remaining prisoners had been transferred to it on Friday. The organization called for its teams to be granted access to the remaining prisoners, noting that it has not had access to detainees held in Israel since October 2023.“Many families in Lebanon are still waiting for answers about the fate of loved ones who may be detained, deceased or otherwise unaccounted for,” it said.
    
        
    

The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a statement Thursday that Israel agreed to release five Lebanese civilians detained by Israeli forces in southern Lebanon after Lebanon provided assistance in searching for the bodies of Lebanese Jewish leaders who were “abducted and murdered by terrorist organizations” in the 1980s, during Lebanon’s civil war.

                                        KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia (AP) — China has arrested 52 Singapore citizens in the southern region of Guangxi in a law enforcement operation targeting suspected pyramid scheme activities and related offenses, Singapore’s Foreign Ministry said Friday.Sim Ann, Singapore’s second minister for foreign affairs, said the city-state is in contact with Chinese authorities to obtain more information on the matter. She said staff from the Singapore Embassy in Beijing have visited the 52 detainees and are providing them with consular support.The ministry said Chinese authorities are continuing their investigations. It didn’t provide details on when the Singaporeans were arrested, their identities or the amount of money involved. In Beijing, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters Friday that China investigates and handles criminal cases involving foreign citizens in accordance with the law. 
    
        
    

Sim said Singapore’s government doesn’t intervene in other countries’ judicial processes and investigations, but that “due process should be accorded to our citizens,” according to a transcript of her remarks on the Foreign Ministry’s website.Sim urged Singaporeans to exercise caution when considering business or investment schemes, especially those involving the recruitment of new participants, the upfront payment of substantial sums of money or promises of unusually high returns.


    
        




    


Pyramid schemes typically require participants to pay to join and recruit others, with financial returns depending largely on bringing in new participants and their payments.

Geopolitics & Diplomacy.title: Myanmar’s Min Aung Hlaing visiting Vietnam as he seeks to normalize relations with ASEAN
Geopolitics & Diplomacy.text:
In this photo released by Myanmar President Office, Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing, right, shakes hands with Commander-in-Chief Gen. Ye Win Oo, left, upon his departure to Vietnam, at the Naypyitaw international airport Friday, Sept. 4, 2026, in Naypyitaw, Myanmar. (Myanmar President Office via AP)2026-09-04T06:09:35Z
                                        BANGKOK (AP) — The leader of Myanmar’s military-backed government is visiting Vietnam for talks with its leaders in his latest effort to normalize relations with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and attract foreign investment.Min Aung Hlaing has stepped up diplomatic engagements since he was sworn in as president in April following an election that critics say was designed to cement the military’s hold on power.Since taking office, he has traveled to India, China, Laos, Thailand and most recently Kazakhstan, Belarus and Russia, where he met with leaders and sought to draw foreign investment through business forums.Vietnam has maintained longstanding military ties with Myanmar, including defense cooperation and the involvement of Viettel, Vietnam’s military-run telecommunications group, in Mytel, one of Myanmar’s major telecom operators, which has military-linked ownership.
    
        
    

Economic ties, however, have weakened, with bilateral trade falling from $853 million in 2020 to $590 million in 2025 and $335 million in the first half of 2026, figures Min Aung Hlaing shared with Vietnam’s Foreign Minister Le Hoai Trung when they met in Myanmar in late August, according to Vietnam’s foreign ministry.State-run MRTV television said Min Aung Hlaing departed on a flight from the capital, Naypyitaw, Friday morning.


    
        




    


In Hanoi, Min Aung Hlaing is expected to meet Vietnamese President To Lam and other senior officials and attend a business forum with members of his Cabinet.The diplomatic outreach is the latest in a series of moves to reengage with countries in the region and the international community after relations became frayed or frosty following Min Aung Hlaing’s ousting of Aung San Suu Kyi’s government in February 2021 while serving as army chief.

Friday’s visit marks Min Aung Hlaing’s third visit to an ASEAN member state as he seeks to restore his standing within the 11-member bloc, of which Myanmar and Vietnam are members.He faced years of diplomatic isolation following his 2021 takeover and was barred from top-level ASEAN meetings for failing to comply with a peace plan agreed upon in April 2021.

Entertainment.title: Maison Margiela's REPLICA Wraps "Lazy Sunday Morning" and "Jazz Club" Scents in Newspaper Print for Its Second Holiday 2026 Offering
Entertainment.text: SummaryMaison Margiela's REPLICA line returns with the second installment of its 2026 holiday collection, led by newspaper-print editions of two signature scentsNew additions include an "Up At Dawn" hand cream and a "By the Fireplace" candle built around wintry scent storiesTwo mix-and-match coffret sets let shoppers pair a fragrance with their choice of body careMaison Margiela's REPLICA fragrance line is expanding its 2026 holiday offering with a second wave, anchored by limited-edition versions of "Lazy Sunday Morning" and "Jazz Club." Both eau de toilettes arrive dressed in a holiday-exclusive newspaper-style print, joined by new body care, a candle, and a pair of customizable gift sets.The two returning scents are the centerpiece, each carried over in its full 100 mL format under the "PRINT SHOP" holiday design. "Lazy Sunday Morning" builds its story around a sunny Sunday in Florence, spent wrapped in freshly laundered linen sheets, and reads as fresh and clean on the skin. "Jazz Club" pulls in the opposite direction, drawing on a private New York jazz club for a warmer, spicier profile that suggests rich cocktails and mellow whiskey for a more intimate, grown-up mood.New to this wave is the "Up At Dawn" hand cream, centered on a dawn-rose scent that opens like fresh roses blooming in a mist-covered garden. The formula does functional work alongside the fragrance, using hyaluronic acid to add moisture while shea butter and almond oil guard against dryness, finishing with a light texture meant to leave hands supple rather than heavy.Rounding out the seasonal additions is the "By the Fireplace" candle, a natural fit for winter. Its scent sets the scene in midwinter Chamonix, France, capturing the crackle of a fireplace and the faint sweetness of chestnut for a warm, enclosed feel.The collection also leans into personalization through two coffret formats. The larger 30 mL Holiday Set lets shoppers choose one 30 mL fragrance from all 14 REPLICA scents, add a body care item of their choice, and take home a 1.2 mL "Jazz Club" mini and a holiday-exclusive shopper. A more compact 10 mL Holiday Set pairs a 10 mL fragrance with a hand cream, with both drawn from a choice of "Lazy Sunday Morning" or "Up At Dawn." Standalone holiday gift versions of "Lazy Sunday Morning" in eau de toilette, hand cream, and lip balm complete the range.The second wave of Maison Margiela REPLICA's 2026 holiday collection goes on sale nationwide October 22, with early availability at select stores from October 15.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: McDonald's Japan Supersizes the Tsukimi Burger Into a 27-Inch Plushie
Entertainment.text: SummaryMcDonald's Japan is running a lottery for a giant Tsukimi Burger plushie tied to the sandwich's 35th anniversaryThe soft toy measures 27.6 inches across and faithfully recreates the burger's signature layersEntry is limited to MyMcDonald's Rewards members and closes in late OctoberMcDonald's Japan is handing fans a chance to win an oversized Tsukimi Burger plushie, celebrating 35 years of one of the chain's most recognizable seasonal sandwiches. First introduced in 1991 as a nod to Japan's fall moon-viewing custom, the Tsukimi Burger now gets a plush tribute built at a scale that will not fit neatly on a shelf.The plushie is the whole point, and it commits to the bit. It measures 27.6 inches, or roughly 70 cm, and recreates the Tsukimi Burger's full stack in soft form, from its signature round egg to a chunky beef patty, smoked bacon, and a layer of creamy tomato sauce. Its soft, fluffy texture leans into the toy angle, making it as much a huggable living-room object as an anniversary keepsake.Getting one takes some work, since it is a lottery prize rather than an item for sale. The plushie is available only to members of the MyMcDonald's Rewards program in Japan. To qualify, customers first register through the official McDonald's Japan app, then purchase three eligible Tsukimi Family sets and spend 250 reward points to submit an entry.The entry period runs from September 2 through October 21, with lottery applications accepted until October 27. Entertainment.title: Michael Jordan's Ferrari That Inspired the Air Jordan XIV Is Heading to Auction Estimated at Up to $1.3M USD
Entertainment.text: SummaryMichael Jordan's custom 1997 Ferrari 550 Maranello is heading to auction for the first time after disappearing from public view for 24 yearsThe V-12 grand tourer famously inspired the design of the Air Jordan XIV and appeared onscreen during the Chicago Bulls' historic championship runPharrell Williams' platform Joopiter expects the cultural artifact to fetch up to $1.3 million in its inaugural automotive saleMichael Jordan's exactingly customized 1997 Ferrari 550 Maranello is stepping back into the spotlight, hitting the auction block for an estimated $700,000 USD to $1,300,000 USD. The monumental sale marks a first for JOOPITER, the sports collectibles platform founded by singer Pharrell Williams, which is operating in partnership with automotive specialist Curated to move its first-ever car. By bridging the world of high-end automotive collecting with the cultural weight of elite sports memorabilia, this auction tests a new ceiling for modern classic valuation.Jordan took delivery of the new vehicle in May 1997, specifically tailoring the Italian powerhouse to his exact aesthetic and physical dimensions. The grand tourer is cloaked in Rosso Barchetta paint, riding on chrome Speedline wheels and concealing a naturally aspirated, 485-hp Ferrari V-12 engine mated to a purist-approved gated manual transmission. To accommodate his six-foot-six frame, Ferrari uniquely modified the tan leather interior by installing longer chair rails and equipping the seats with slimmer padding. In a move of calculated understatement, Jordan also ordered the car entirely without the traditional yellow Ferrari fender shields.The coupe's provenance is inextricably tied to peak Chicago Bulls dominance. Jordan famously drove the car out of the United Center with an Illinois vanity plate reading "MJ 5" on June 13, 1997, immediately after clinching his fifth NBA Championship. The vehicle was later seen rolling out of a January 1998 practice in the seminal ESPN documentary The Last Dance. Its cultural footprint extends far beyond the pavement, directly shaping sneaker history when the vehicle inspired Nike VP of Design Tinker Hatfield to create the Air Jordan XIV basketball shoe. Hatfield pulled directly from the Italian bodywork, integrating a Ferrari-like yellow-and-black Jumpman shield and a heavy tire-tread sole pattern into the iconic silhouette.Jordan ultimately sold the Ferrari at the end of 2002, inadvertently kicking off a decades-long vanishing act. The legendary chassis remained completely out of public view for 24 years before being definitively rediscovered in 2026. Despite its mythic status and sheer performance capabilities, the vehicle has been driven sparingly across its entire lifespan, showing just under 19,000 miles on the odometer as it heads to its historic Joopiter sale.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Jin Sakai Returns as a Playable Fighter in ‘Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted’
Entertainment.text: SummaryJin Sakai, the hero of 'Ghost of Tsushima,' has been revealed as a playable character in the new 'Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted' modeMost Wanted is a single-player roguelike built around bounty runs, unlockable perks, and four distinct fightersThe mode arrives alongside the narrative expansion 'Echoes of Sekigahara' as part of 'Ghost of Yōtei' Complete EditionJin Sakai is back. Sucker Punch has revealed that the Ghost of Tsushima protagonist joins Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted as a playable character, carrying over all four of his signature combat stances. Shown during the September 3 State of Play, his return anchors a brand-new roguelike mode landing inside Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition on October 1.Sucker Punch built Jin’s return as a faithful bridge between games. The team took his Ghost of Tsushima model and preserved it while applying upgrades for Ghost of Yōtei, keeping all four of the original stances so players can once again shift between them to exploit enemy weaknesses. He starts with a Sticky Bomb and a hankyu, and his kit leans on returning signatures: his Ultimate is the "Dance of Wrath" skill that targets and disarms multiple enemies, while his Kill Streak is, fittingly, Ghost Stance, letting him terrify nearby foes and cut down a limited number in single hits. The nod runs deep, given that Jin headlined Sucker Punch's 2020 predecessor before Atsu took over the Ghost mantle in Ezo.Around him sits the structure of Most Wanted itself, pitched as the studio's spin on the roguelike. Runs begin at a bounty board, where each target is a member of the Yōtei Six, reached only by clearing waves of enemies and minibosses. Finishing waves unlocks perks that shape an increasingly powerful build toward the bounty's final boss, and cleared bounties can be replayed at higher difficulty, culminating in the toughest run against Lord Saito. Between runs, players spend earned Mon on techniques, weapon upgrades, charms, and character unlocks, and any cosmetics earned carry back into the main game. Perks are framed as the real engine of the mode, with frequent choices spanning weapon mastery, gear loadouts, summons, parries, and survivability that reward experimentation.The default fighter is Atsu, who wields dual katana and two Ghost Tools, with a "Call of the Pack" Ultimate that summons wolves. Oyuki fights with the kusarigama, kunai, and tanegashima rifle, backed by a "Shadow Killer" Ultimate. Nagato covers distance with a yari, tanzutsu pistol, and both long and short bows, and his "Gambler's Mark" Ultimate fires guaranteed headshots. Each character opens with a katana plus their own weapons, abilities, Ultimates, and Kill Streaks, encouraging players to test every approach.The same release also expands the story through Echoes of Sekigahara. The expansion splits between two chapters of Atsu's life, her time on the mainland during the massive Battle of Sekigahara and the present day, filling in her history with Nagato. In the present, Nagato reaches Ezo hunted by the Vipers, a group of vicious poachers loyal to the Snake and left leaderless after his death, who have overrun the previously unseen Ashoro Foothills. Atsu reluctantly teams with Nagato to recover a captured ally, encountering new enemy types, heavy weapons, mythic tales, abilities, and armor along the way.Both drops mark a milestone, arriving as Ghost of Yōtei reaches its one-year anniversary. They headline the Complete Edition, which bundles the original game, the Legends co-op mode, and previously released Digital Deluxe content, while a free October 1 patch hands all existing owners extras including the new Beauty of Yōtei photo mode, fresh Watanabe Mode tracks, and a high-contrast accessibility option.Ghost of Yōtei: Most Wanted and Echoes of Sekigahara launch October 1 as part of Ghost of Yōtei Complete Edition, with existing owners able to pre-order the upgrade now and pre-orders by September 30 unlocking early access to the Sakai Armor for Atsu.Read more at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Square Enix Sets April 2027 Release Date for ‘Final Fantasy VII Revelation’
Entertainment.text: SummarySquare Enix has dated 'Final Fantasy VII Revelation,' the conclusion of its Remake project, with a new trailer and gameplay shown during PlayStation's State of PlayThe finale introduces a fully open world traversed by the Highwind airship, alongside new systems and playable charactersThe story sends Cloud and his companions toward a final confrontation with Sephiroth as the planet faces total destructionSquare Enix has set Final Fantasy VII Revelation, the closing chapter of its sprawling Remake project, for release on April 8, 2027. Revealed during PlayStation's State of Play with a fresh trailer and an extended gameplay deep dive, the finale arrives across PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Steam, the Epic Games Store, and Xbox on PC.The headline change is scale. Revelation opens the planet into a genuinely borderless world, letting players roam every corner aboard the series' iconic Highwind airship. Traversal gets its own companion in Piko, a Chocobo that grows alongside the party and picks up new movement and combat abilities over time, while a new grappling gun lets characters scale rooftops and zip through the environment at speed.Combat builds on the hybrid system the trilogy is known for, now reshaped by the new FITS system. FITS grants abilities and higher tiers of power through specialized roles, including Warrior, Knight, Black Mage, and Summoner, with the extended footage showing new playable character Cid in the Knight FITS and returning fan favorite Vincent in the Summoner FITS. Beyond the two additions to the roster, players can freely swap their active character and rework the party at any point during exploration, and can steer the narrative by choosing which members take on specific quests, changing how certain events play out.All of that flexibility feeds into a story pitched as the end of the line. Cloud Strife and his companions face a world on the edge of annihilation, grieving a fallen ally as Sephiroth closes in on godhood. The party takes to the skies aboard the Highwind in a race to stop Meteor, the ultimate destructive magic, before it wipes out the planet entirely.The finale also caps a trilogy that arrived with heavy expectations and largely met them. The first two entries, Final Fantasy VII Remake and Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, drew wide acclaim, together collecting more than 140 perfect review scores along with Game of the Year recognition. For newcomers or lapsed fans, both remain available with a Streamlined Progression option, offering tweaks like unlimited HP and MP and an always-full ATB gauge to ease the catch-up, and save data from either game unlocks bonus summons and weapon skins in Revelation.Final Fantasy VII Revelation launches April 8, 2027 on PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S, and PC, with physical and digital pre-orders open now (digital Nintendo Switch 2 pre-orders to follow) at global retailers and the Square Enix Store.Read more at Hypebeast

Alfonso Cuarón joined the production as an executive producer, while John August signed on to serve as both a core writer and an executive producer. Hasbro Entertainment also develops the project alongside these producers to ensure the property carries weight.For decades, the source material has commanded respect in the gaming community as one of the most iconic campaign settings in Dungeons & Dragons, Ravenloft. This atmospheric universe provides a textured canvas for a premium adaptation. The television project specifically adapts the classic tabletop setting to capitalize on a renewed interest in the franchise's darker dimensions. Development of the show aligns with a modern revitalization of the lore following the release of Ravenloft: The Horrors Within. Narrative themes prioritize the psychology of a legendary antagonist over traditional action.The narrative centers strictly on the origins of the most famous vampire in Dungeons & Dragons, Strahd von Zarovich. This character has terrorized campaigns for generations as an enigmatic force. The upcoming series humanizes the backstory of the villain by offering a look at the man before the monster. Intense plot points focus on his pursuit of power, his experiences with love and the blinding obsession that ultimately dictates his fate.The series explores the undead transformation of the protagonist with narrative depth. Its overarching story charts a journey from a tragic antihero into a bloodthirsty vampire Darklord. This evolution ensures the adaptation is steeped in tragedy and complex character dynamics. The Netflix production anchors its central conflict entirely around this dark metamorphosis.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Buffer Drags ‘Fast Times at Ridgemont High’ Into a Capsule Ruled by "No Shirts, No Shoes, No Dice"
Entertainment.text: SummaryBuffer, the label helmed by creative director Tetsu Nishiyama and operated by HUMAN MADE, has teamed with the 1982 American teen movie for a graphics-led collectionThe collaboration runs to three T-shirt styles, each filtering the film through Buffer's own design lensA set of Buffer original pieces rounds out the release, including a long-sleeve T-shirt that reworks the brand's main logoBuffer, the brand led by creative director Tetsu Nishiyama and operated by HUMAN MADE, is releasing a collaboration collection with Fast Times at Ridgemont High, the 1982 American high-school comedy. The capsule reads the film's world through Buffer's graphic sensibility, landing as a tight run of T-shirts rather than a sprawling licensing exercise.The collaboration centers on three T-shirt designs, each taking a different route into the source material. One is handled by illustrator Naoki Shoji, who builds his piece around the movie as a motif. A second prints a run of the film's memorable scenes directly onto the shirt, leaning on recognizable imagery. The third distills the movie down to a single line, translating its emblematic rule "NO SHIRTS, NO SHOES, NO DICE" into a standalone graphic.That three-way split is where the technical intent shows. Rather than slapping a single still on a blank, Buffer treats the film as raw material to be reinterpreted, moving from illustration to photographic scene print to text-driven graphic across the set. It is a small collection built to cover distinct graphic registers instead of repeating one idea in different colors.The film crossover also fits a longer pattern for the label. Buffer has built a throughline of movie-referencing capsules, and pairing with a 1982 teen comedy slots neatly into a graphic language rooted in American pop-culture nostalgia. Fast Times at Ridgemont High carries a specific early-80s Americana that maps onto Nishiyama's ongoing interest in vintage US reference points, giving the T-shirts a cultural anchor beyond the artwork itself.Alongside the collaboration, Buffer is offering its own originals in the same drop. Entertainment.title: The LEGO PlayStation Rebuilds the Original 1994 Console in 1,911 Bricks With Working Buttons
Entertainment.text: SummarySony and the LEGO Group have revealed the LEGO PlayStation, a brick replica of the original console and controllerThe 1,911-piece build recreates the hardware at close to 1:1 scale and folds in functional details and hidden nods to PlayStation historyTwo removable game dioramas tied to Ape Escape and Gran Turismo extend the set into a display piece marking 30 years of the platformSony and the LEGO Group have unveiled the LEGO PlayStation, a buildable replica of the original PlayStation console and controller shown during the September 3 State of Play. It is the first time fans can construct the debut hardware brick by brick, arriving as a tribute to a platform that has been in players' hands for more than three decades.The set runs to 1,911 pieces and lands at a near 1:1 recreation of the console, measuring 10.5 inches, or 26 cm, wide once fully assembled. Rather than a static shelf model, it carries functional mechanisms: the Power and Open buttons work, and the included controller can plug into the console, giving the finished piece a layer of interactivity beyond the display.Working with LEGO designers, PlayStation built the assembly around its own origins, tucking hidden references to the platform's history into the process. Two of those references become their own modules, pulling in a pair of games that launched on the original console. The Gran Turismo diorama includes a miniature track with scaled-down cars, while the Ape Escape diorama sets up a nostalgic island scene with a swappable blue or red light on the monkey's helmet. Both dioramas can be removed and displayed on their own, and each carries customizable elements, so the set functions as three connected pieces rather than one fixed sculpture.By recreating the 1994 hardware and threading in Ape Escape and Gran Turismo, the set reaches back to the era that defined the brand's first generation, aiming squarely at players who have followed PlayStation since launch as much as newer fans. The result positions the LEGO PlayStation less as a toy and more as a physical marker of the platform's 30-plus-year run, built to sit on a shelf as a piece of console history.The LEGO PlayStation goes on sale via the PlayStation webstore and for LEGO Insiders Early Access starting October 1, then reaches the LEGO webstore and LEGO Stores on October 4.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Climate & Environment.text:
Kuching riverside in the city center is shrouded in thick haze in Kuching, Sarawak state, Malaysia, Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. (AP Photo/Xpin Voon)2026-09-04T09:05:02Z
                                        KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia (AP) — Malaysia declared an emergency Friday in a town in Sarawak state on Borneo Island after air pollution breached the country’s emergency-level threshold linked to fires in neighboring Indonesia.The Air Pollutant Index in Serian, a small agricultural town of just under 90,000 near the border of Indonesia’s Kalimantan province, surged to 521 on Friday, according to Malaysia’s environment department. Sarawak’s much-larger capital, Kuching, also showed a hazardous reading of 311.Malaysia’s King Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar has consented to the declaration of an emergency in Serian, which would allow more effective measures to be taken, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s office said in a statement. It didn’t provide details but officials have said a reading above 500 could provide for nonessential work and outdoor activities to be halted. Schools are already shut if the index is above 200. 
    
        
    

Haze is a recurring seasonal problem in Southeast Asia, where smoke from forest and peat fires in Indonesia can travel across national borders and affect neighboring Malaysia, Brunei and Singapore.Sarawak has been the worst-hit Malaysian state by the haze, with several areas having hazardous air levels in the past few days. 


    
        




    


The haze this year has been particularly severe, with elevated fire activity in several provinces in Indonesia, including Kalimantan, and prolonged dry conditions contributing to worsening pollution across parts of Borneo.Satellite data from Indonesia’s Forestry Ministry on Friday detected 717 hot spots nationwide likely caused by forest fires since Aug. 1. The data showed 103 active hot spots in the past 24 hours alone.

Sports.title: Duo standing 7-foot-3 and 6-10 will have teams looking up to China at women’s FIBA World Cup
Sports.text:
Han Xu of China practices during a training session ahead of the match between China and United States during the Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, Germany, Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026. (AP Photo/Ebrahim Noroozi)2026-09-04T04:00:14Z
                                        BERLIN (AP) — Opponents will be looking up to China during the women’s FIBA World Cup, starting with the the United States.The Americans and everyone else will have to navigate around and over some of the tallest women on the planet: China’s 19-year-old Zhang Ziyu stands 7-foot-3. The U.S. team is already familiar with 6-10 Han Xu from her WNBA games with the New York Liberty.If not for a passport mishap, Zhang and Han would be joined by another center — 6-7 Li Yueru, who plays with the WNBA’s Dallas Wings. Li posted on social media Wednesday that her passport was lost in the mail and she won’t be able to compete.China opens its campaign against the four-time defending champion in Berlin on Friday.
    
        
    

Tournament will be Zhang’s world debutZhang wasn’t playing when the U.S. beat China 83-61 in the 2022 World Cup final in Sydney for a fourth consecutive gold medal. She made her senior debut at the Women’s Asia Cup last year and helped China capture the bronze, averaging 14.8 points and 5.5 rebounds in the tournament.Han praised her performance at that tournament and said she was ready to step onto the world stage.“World Cup is a good moment for her, for the whole world to know her,” Han told The Associated Press. “I am so excited to play with her again.”


    
        




    


Both of Zhang’s parents played basketball and it was her mother who encouraged her to take up the sport.As one of the oldest players in the Chinese roster at 26, Han takes on the responsibly of looking out for her younger teammates. She points out that Zhang is still “very young” and just starting her career.“She’s a little girl, you know, like the heart is soft,” she said.
    
        
            
                
                    
    
    


    

  

  
    Read More 
  
  

    
    
    
  

    
        
    

                
            
        
    
If Zhang plays on Friday — she missed China’s pre-tournament warmup against France on Tuesday and wasn’t practicing during the brief time-slots open to media Wednesday and Thursday — her height alone will ensure she stands out against the tournament favorites.“She’s good,” Han said on Wednesday. “She just needs some rest ... she has (a) big body and tall girl, and she needs some time to rest a little bit.” 
    
        
    

On Thursday she said Zhang had practiced “a little bit” earlier before the media was allowed in.U.S. guard Sonia Citron, also making her World Cup debut, says they’ll be prepared either way.“I think just try to make it difficult for her, you know, to guard her as a team,” Citron said. “Just don’t leave anybody on an island, but yeah, I think we’ll prep everything and then be ready.”China’s ambitions for the World CupFew expect China to go further than it did in 2022, with France and Australia expected to be most likely challengers for the U.S.. But Zhang’s introduction gives the Chinese an extra weapon they didn’t have four years ago.“At the last World Cup, we played our best, but before we played, we never thought we would do so well, but we gave 100%,” Han said.. “I’ll try to do the same or better and try to focus every single game. “Especially me, I just try to focus because there’s so much noise around me.”___ AP Basketball Writer Doug Feinberg contributed to this report. ___See AP’s full WNBA coverage here
